concept.name: Analysis error
concept.definition: A flaw in the reasoning or information processing behind a trade - misread trend, wrong level, ignored evidence, miscalibrated probability - as distinct from an execution mistake or a risk-management breach. It is the error class that review and education, rather than checklists, must fix.
concept.intuition: You did exactly what you planned; the problem is the plan was built on a misread chart.
concept.mechanics: Identified in post-trade and decision-journal review by comparing the recorded thesis with the information available at the time: cognitive biases (confirmation, anchoring, recency), data errors, and logical gaps are the usual culprits. Persistent analysis errors point to gaps in market understanding or to a systematic bias.
concept.failure_modes: Hindsight bias makes analysis errors hard to diagnose honestly - the misread is rewritten as nearly right. Small samples confound signal: a correct analysis can lose and a wrong one can win several times in a row.
concept.misconceptions: A losing trade is not automatically an analysis error - sound analysis of a probabilistic setup still loses its share of times. Conversely, a winning trade built on misread information is still an analysis error, not validation.
concept.example: A trader shorts into what he reads as distribution, ignoring that the decline is on falling volume into a major demand zone; review tags it as an analysis error: context filter omitted.

citations.source: Brett N. Steenbarger, The Psychology of Trading: Tools and Techniques for Minding the Markets (Wiley, 2003) - publisher page
